definition: Bucolic means relating to the pleasant, peaceful life of the countryside.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word bucolic. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know bucolic should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: They planned the whole cycling trip around one bucolic valley — sheep bells, cider stands, and lanes with grass growing down the middle.
Rural is the plain map-word — it stops well short of bucolic, promising countryside but saying nothing about whether the countryside is pleasant.
Arcadian goes further than bucolic, leaving real farmland behind for a countryside so perfect it exists only in poems and myths.

Pastoral is the countryside as art frames it — shepherds, flocks, and green hills arranged in a painting, poem, or symphony. Bucolic praises the pleasant, peaceful countryside itself, no frame required: a real lane with real sheep bells. Pastoral describes the depiction; bucolic describes the place and its calm.

Idyllic means blissfully perfect, and it can attach to anything at all — a beach week, a childhood, a summer job. Bucolic is bliss of one particular kind: the pleasant, peaceful life of the countryside. A bucolic valley is usually idyllic, but an idyllic penthouse is nowhere near bucolic.

Greek boukolos, 'cowherd,' walked into English inside this one word and nowhere else — no cousins survive. So there is nothing to peel off and reuse: learn bucolic whole, as the poets' word for the peaceful herding countryside.
Bucolic means relating to the pleasant, peaceful life of the countryside.
The composer kept a photograph of a bucolic scene above her desk — a shepherd dozing against a haystack — and swore the entire second movement was in it.
Bucolic is more precise than 'rural' or 'pretty' because it bundles the countryside together with peace and contentment.
A muddy feedlot is rural; a hillside of grazing sheep at dusk is bucolic.
Bucolic praises the countryside as a place of peace — travel writing, paintings, memories.
For the plain fact of being outside the city, 'rural' does the work without the glow.
Note what bucolic is not: it is about pastures and quiet, so a thrilling wilderness of cliffs and rapids is scenic, not bucolic.
